A fails on baseball, B on weight lifting, and C on pole vault: pole position is from motor racing, not pole vault.

questions.text: Shown below is an image made from line segments. Identify the element, from the options at right, which is NOT part of the image.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: Every shape in the image starts from the centre point: bowl shapes (two arcs meeting at the centre, closed by a straight chord) and pointed petals, repeated around the centre. Options A, B and D are made only of such bowls and petals sharing one tip. Option C has a square whose bottom edge passes through the tip; no straight line in the image runs through the centre like that (the straight lines near the centre are bowl chords that stay clear of it), so C is not part of the image.

questions.text:
A language reveals the attitudes of the people who use and shape it. And a whole declension of ____(i)____ terminology can be found in the language in which inter-racial relations have been described inside Britain. At first, we were told, the goal was 'integration'. Now this word rapidly came to mean '____(ii)____': a black man could only become integrated when he started behaving like a white one. After 'integration' came the ____(iii)____ of 'racial harmony'. Now once again, this sounded virtuous and desirable, but what it meant in practice was that blacks should be persuaded to live peaceably with whites, in spite of all the injustices done to them every day. The call for 'racial harmony' was simply an invitation to shut up and smile while nothing was done about our grievances. And now there's a new catchword: 'multiculturalism'. In our schools, this means little more than teaching the kids a few bongo rhythms, how to tie a sari and so forth. In the police training programme, it means telling cadets that black people are so 'culturally different' that they can't help making trouble. Multiculturalism is the latest token gesture towards Britain's blacks; and it ought to be exposed, like 'integration' and 'racial harmony', for the ____(iv)____ it is.

In the above passage identify the missing words. The table below contains possible words for each blank. Choose one word from each column for the 4 blanks.

| (i) | (ii) | (iii) | (iv) |
|---|---|---|---|
| astounding | organization | time | sham |
| worrisome | consolidation | place | joy |
| patronizing | assimilation | opportunity | truth |
| critical | association | concept | law |

Read the following paragraph and answer the question that follows.

The correct answer is:
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: The writer is scornful of each official word, so (i) is patronizing terminology. 'Integration' came to mean assimilation, since a black man was integrated only when he behaved like a white one (ii). 'Racial harmony' is described as an idea, the concept (iii). Multiculturalism is a token gesture to be exposed for the sham it is (iv). So the answer is patronizing, assimilation, concept, sham.

questions.text:
The most ____(i)____ respect in which ideas have helped mankind is numbers. There must have been a time when homo sapiens was a very rare species, subsisting precariously in jungles and caves, terrified of wild beasts, having difficulty in securing nourishment. At this period the biological advantage of his greater intelligence, which was cumulative because it could be handed on from generation to generation, had scarcely begun to outweigh the disadvantages of his long infancy, his lessened ____(ii)____ as compared with monkeys, and his lack of ____(iii)____ protection against cold. In those days, the number of men must certainly have been very small. The main use to which, throughout the ages, men have put their technical skill has been ____(iv)____ the total population. I do not mean that this was the intention, but that it was, in fact, the effect. If this is something to rejoice in, then we have occasion to rejoice.

In the above passage identify the missing words. The table below contains possible words for each blank. Choose one word from each column for the 4 blanks.

| (i) | (ii) | (iii) | (iv) |
|---|---|---|---|
| equivocal | freedom | hirsute | increase |
| inconclusive | agility | stubbled | decrease |
| indubitable | confidence | feathery | endanger |
| uncertain | appetite | unshaven | extol |

Read the following paragraph and answer the question that follows.

The correct answer is
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: The writer says numbers are the clearest case of ideas helping mankind, so (i) is indubitable (beyond doubt). Compared with monkeys, early humans had lessened agility (ii) and lacked hirsute (hairy) protection against cold (iii). Since men were once few and are now many, technical skill has served to increase the total population (iv), which is why he speaks of rejoicing.

questions.text: On the left hand side are pieces of a jigsaw puzzle. Identify the image that can be reproduced using all the pieces shown at left.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: There are five pieces: a triangle with one concave curved side, a thin right-angled triangle, a four-sided piece with a right-angled corner, a piece with one convex curved edge, and a right-angled triangle. In A the five regions are a corner right triangle, the region above the arc (convex curve), the triangle under the arc (concave curve), a large four-sided region at bottom left and a thin right triangle at bottom right, matching every piece. B has a thin four-sided strip in place of the large four-sided piece, and C and D have different curves and regions.

questions.text: Choose the set of operations (not necessarily in order) that can be applied on form A to get form B?

options.label: A
options.text: Cut vertically, Taper, Cut at an angle, Bend, Twist

options.label: B
options.text: Cut horizontally, Bend, Cut at an angle, Taper, Twist

options.label: C
options.text: Cut vertically, Stretch, Twist, Bend, Cut at an angle

options.label: D
options.text: Cut vertically, Twist, Stretch, Cut at an angle, Fold

questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Form B has a triangular cross-section, so the square bar was cut vertically along its diagonal. It gets thinner towards the bottom (taper), curves (bend), turns about its own length (twist) and has a slanted top face (cut at an angle). Option A lists exactly these. B starts with a horizontal cut, which cannot give a triangular section, and C and D use stretch or fold instead of taper.

questions.text: Identify the most accurate shadow of the object given below. The arrow indicates direction of light.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A flat shape casts a shadow that is stretched or squashed but keeps the order and relative size of features along each edge. The object's right edge has, from the top, a small round bite, then a larger round bite, then a rounded convex corner. Option A shows the same sequence with similar proportions. B makes the first bite almost vanish, C makes the two bites alike, and D turns the first bite into a long shallow curve.

questions.text: At left is an empty glass with a straw in it. From the options given, identify the correct representation of the straw when the glass is half-filled with water.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Seen through the side of a glass of water, the part of the straw under water looks displaced sideways and slightly thicker, because light bends as it leaves the water and the curved glass acts like a lens. So the straw appears broken at the water surface, with the lower part shifted and magnified, as in A. B shows no change, and C and D do not show the sideways shift with magnification.

questions.text: If the given flat shape is revolved about the Y axis by 360°, identify the solid shape that will be generated.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The top part of the shape stands away from the axis, so revolving it makes a hollow tube with a hole on top (C, with a solid top, is out). The arm with a downward lip makes the wide disc, the two half-circles make two rings, and a short straight stretch of stem shows below the rings. The bottom part touches the axis and has a sharp point, so it makes a solid with a flat top, a sharp edge and a cone down to a small cylinder. A shows the stem below the rings and the sharp edge; B has a rounded edge and D has the rings sitting directly on the flat top.

questions.text: Shown below are schematic diagrams of a regular door latch. X represents the door, and Y represents the frame in the wall. Identify which latch can be used for correctly locking the door.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: To lock, the bolt slides left into the box on frame Y and the handle drops into the second slot so the bolt cannot slide back. The handle moves with the bolt, so the guides must not block it. In B the handle can slide left to the left slot without reaching the left guide, the bolt tip then passes into the frame box, and the bolt's right end stays inside the right guides. In A and C a guide sits in the handle's path, and in D the second slot is on the right, so moving the handle there pulls the bolt away from the frame.

questions.text: Pick a point on the outermost ring of the maze shown below, in order to find your way home. Each point indicates the direction of your next move. Which point on the outermost ring should be your starting point in order to reach home in the fewest steps?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Follow each start. From NE (bottom middle) move north-east to the inner N point, then north to the inner W point, then west into Home: 3 moves. From the W corner you go west to SW, south-west to the inner SW point and then round a loop that never reaches Home. From the N corner and from NW you also end in loops. So NE is the starting point.

questions.text: Shown below is a triangular prism cut into two parts, P and Q. Identify which option represents part P.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: Part P is the piece left when Q is lifted out of the prism, so its surface must fit Q's exactly: every raised part of one is a hollow in the other. Turn P over and match the profile of the cut, step by step, against each option, checking the depth of each step and which face it runs along. Option B matches the cut; the others differ in the depth or position of a step.
